scenes.title: Besnard [boxeur]
scenes.description: A press photograph from 1912 by Agence Rol showing the boxer Besnard, held in the Estampes et photographie department of the Bibliothèque nationale de France (EI-13 (136)). It is a negative on glass measuring 13 x 18 cm, in the public domain and part of the Pho20Rol documentary set.
scenes.explanation: Protective plastic mouthguards for boxing were not developed or worn until the 1970s, so this object cannot exist in a 1912 photograph.

source.description: Référence bibliographique : Rol, 18463 Appartient à l’ensemble documentaire : Pho20Rol

scenes.credit: Agence Rol. Agence photographique (commanditaire) via Bibliothèque nationale de France (Gallica)

scenes.title: Les mutilés de l'armée : un aveugle gravant
scenes.description: A photograph from the Agence Meurisse press agency, dated 1915, shows a blind wounded soldier from the army engraving. It belongs to the Bibliothèque nationale de France (department of prints and photographs) and is titled "Les mutilés de l'armée : un aveugle gravant" ("The mutilated of the army: a blind man engraving").
scenes.explanation: A battery-powered LED lamp cannot exist in 1915 because practical visible-light LEDs were only developed in the 1960s.

scenes.title: Majorstua
scenes.description: A photograph from Majorstua in 1959, held by the National Library of Norway and in the public domain.
scenes.explanation: Plastic road barriers did not exist in 1959; they were developed later as a lightweight alternative to metal and wooden barriers.
scenes.credit: Mittet & Co. AS, Brun, Jac via National Library of Norway

scenes.title: 14-10-20, stade Brancion [groupe de spectateurs]
scenes.description: A press photograph by Agence Rol showing a group of spectators at the Brancion stadium in Paris, dated 14 October 1920. The record identifies it as a glass negative held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France.
scenes.explanation: Telescoping aluminum selfie sticks did not exist in 1920; they became common consumer accessories only in the 1980s and later.
